name: QILIN

variants.depicted: The LIN in the Shuowen description quoted by the Kangxi Dictionary: the five-coloured benevolent composite beast with yellow belly, ox tail, wolf forehead and horse hooves.
variants.anatomy: ONE complete living quadruped, one head, two eyes, FOUR legs with HORSE hooves, a roe-deer-like body, a broad distinctly WOLF-like forehead, ONE long OX tail with tuft. FIVE natural fur colours distributed in irregular tactile patches: muted black, off-white, red-brown, blue-grey, and yellow-gold, with a clearly YELLOW belly. It is a large staglike composite creature, height recorded as zhang-two. The selected c07 description does NOT specify a horn: render a plain brow with NO invented antlers or added dragon horn. No dragon scales, flames, wings, tusks or armour. [qilin-c07]
variants.moment: Bound toward the near viewer in an energetic protective movement, one horse-hoofed foreleg raised and the other driving onto the near ground; head lowered just enough to make the wolf forehead and steady commanding eyes immense. Benevolent but overwhelming, no snarling fangs or cruelty.
variants.power: No documented supernatural visual power. Its extraordinary mixed anatomy, documented large stature and movement supply sacred awe; small dust and shifting pebbles only from physical hoof impact. No fire, magic glow or rainbow energy. [qilin-c07, qilin-c08]
variants.setting: A rough natural hunting ground at Daye, where the lin was recorded in the Zuo Zhuan hunt. No hunters or weapons in image; the landscape is cropped closely and secondary. [qilin-c12]
variants.camera: Low close three-quarter confrontation, head/wolf-forehead and two front HORSE HOOVES are very large, body and yellow underside visible diagonally, OX tail with tuft readable at side. No ordinary deer grazing pose.
variants.light: One warm low afternoon shaft lights the coloured natural fur and yellow underside against deep walnut earth shadow.

requirements.description: Exact c07 Shuowen Lin source variant: roe-deer body, ox tail, wolf forehead, horse hooves, five colours/yellow belly and documented stature. Horn is unspecified so no extra horn added as editorial restraint.
No supernatural visual power; benevolent protective movement and dust only from hoof contact.
Daye hunting ground, without staging capture or hunters.

variants.prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of QILIN. The LIN in the Shuowen description quoted by the Kangxi Dictionary: the five-coloured benevolent composite beast with yellow belly, ox tail, wolf forehead and horse hooves.
ANATOMY: ONE complete living quadruped, one head, two eyes, FOUR legs each ending in ONE SOLID ROUND HORSE HOOF, absolutely NO cloven/split hoof or toe cleft; smooth continuous semicircular keratin hoof walls like a real horse. A clearly lean roe-deer BODY with short natural fur, deer-shaped narrow muzzle and only the broad FOREHEAD/BROW of a WOLF, not an entire wolf face or wolf body, ONE long OX tail with tuft. FIVE natural fur colours distributed in irregular tactile patches: muted black, off-white, red-brown, blue-grey, and yellow-gold, with a clearly YELLOW belly. It is a large staglike composite creature, height recorded as zhang-two. The selected c07 description does NOT specify a horn: render a plain brow with NO invented antlers or added dragon horn. No dragon scales, flames, wings, tusks or armour. [qilin-c07]
MOMENT: Bound toward the near viewer in an energetic protective movement, one horse-hoofed foreleg raised and the other driving onto the near ground; head lowered just enough to make the wolf forehead and steady commanding eyes immense. Benevolent but overwhelming, no mane, thick canine neck, wolf body or snarling fangs or cruelty.
POWER: No documented supernatural visual power. Its extraordinary mixed anatomy, documented large stature and movement supply sacred awe; small dust and shifting pebbles only from physical hoof impact. No fire, magic glow or rainbow energy. [qilin-c07, qilin-c08]
SCALE & CAMERA: Low close three-quarter confrontation, head/wolf-forehead and two front HORSE HOOVES are very large, body and yellow underside visible diagonally, OX tail with tuft readable at side. No ordinary deer grazing pose.
LIGHT & WEATHER: One warm low afternoon shaft lights the coloured natural fur and yellow underside against deep walnut earth shadow.
SURFACE: Tactile natural fur, fish/serpent scales, hoof, feathers or stone as specified; premium traditional painterly brushwork, never glossy plastic or a toy.
SETTING: A rough natural hunting ground at Daye, where the lin was recorded in the Zuo Zhuan hunt. No hunters or weapons in image; the landscape is cropped closely and secondary. [qilin-c12]
MOOD: overwhelming and imposing sacred presence; respectful, benevolent when source says so, energetic and majestic, never cute, calm or decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: one square original illustration; no text, labels, lettering, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra limbs, heads, tails or digits beyond exact counts above; no nudity or gore; no design from a film, game, anime or comic; no generic glow aura, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or unsupported supernatural effects. Identifying anatomical components all readable at thumbnail size.
CRITICAL SOURCE CORRECTION: Each foot must be an UNDIVIDED HORSE HOOF, not the CLOVEN paired toes of a deer, cow or goat. Make the body slender roe-deer anatomy and the forehead wolf-like while retaining a narrow deer-shaped muzzle. NO animal mane. The last attempt failed because all hooves were visibly cloven and body too canine.

variants.depicted: The QI of Shuowen quoted by Kangxi: benevolent deer-bodied ox-tailed beast with exactly ONE horn, not Guo Pu's hornless version.

No antlers, paired horns, wolf forehead, lion mane, dragon scales, five-colour requirement, wings, fire or armour. This is specifically the Shuowen QI one-horn description in c10, NOT Guo Pu's separate hornless interpretation. Natural dark warm brown fur; palette artistic. [qilin-c10]
variants.moment: Leap diagonally upward toward the foreground across the rough natural ground, front legs lifted distinctly, rear hooves pushing off, tail sweeping fully across one side. Turn the proud head toward us with an intense wise gaze, single horn fully silhouetted.
variants.power: No supernatural power effect, no flame or elemental control. Sacred overwhelming presence comes from the exact composite anatomy and dynamic approach of the benevolent beast. Physically scattered earth from the leap is small and plausible. [qilin-c10]
variants.setting: Tight natural dark earth-and-rock background as neutral editorial staging; no invented temple, palace, ritual or named habitat claim.
variants.camera: Full-body broad diagonal low-angle composition, beast occupies eighty-five percent of square with ALL FOUR legs, OX tail and ONE central horn readable. Ordinary body size through near-camera framing, not invented cosmic giant.
variants.light: One strong dying-sun sidelight, rich dark walnut and antique gold accents in the natural fur and hoof texture.

rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
